summary: Some mitzvos have parts that do not hold each other back: the techeles and white strings of tzitzis, the tefillin of the arm and the head, the flour and oil and the wine, and the placings of blood on the outer mizbeach.

chunks.en: The techeles does not hold back the white,
chunks.st: The absence of the sky-blue [tekhelet] strings does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva of ritual fringes with the white strings,

chunks.en: and the white does not hold back the techeles.
chunks.st: and the absence of white strings does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva with the sky-blue strings. If one has only one, he wears it without the other.

chunks.en: The tefillin of the arm
chunks.st: Absence of the phylacteries of the arm

chunks.en: does not hold back the one of the head,
chunks.st: does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva of the phylacteries of the head,

chunks.he: וְשֶׁל ראשׁ אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת שֶׁל יָד.
chunks.en: and the one of the head does not hold back the one of the arm.
chunks.st: and absence of the phylacteries of the head does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva of the phylacteries of the arm. If one has only one, he dons it without the other.
chunks.stMore: The mishna returns to discussing the halakhot of meal offerings, which are the central theme of this tractate.

chunks.he: הַסֹּלֶת וְהַשֶּׁמֶן אֵינָם מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַיַּיִן,
chunks.en: The flour and the oil do not hold back the wine,
chunks.st: The absence of the fine flour and the oil for the meal offering accompanying burnt offerings and peace offerings does not prevent libation of the wine,

chunks.en: and the wine does not hold them back.
chunks.st: and the absence of the wine for libation does not prevent sacrifice of the flour and the oil.

chunks.en: The placings of blood on the outer mizbeach
chunks.st: Failure to perform some of the placements of blood on the external altar

words.note: Putting the korban's blood on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: do not hold each other back.
chunks.st: does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva with the other
chunks.stMore: placements, as even if the priest performed only one placement of blood, the offering effects atonement after the fact.

summary: On Yom Tov many animals are brought for the musaf, and missing one does not hold back the others. Rabbi Shimon says that if there is not enough money for the nesachim of all the bulls, it is better to bring one bull with its nesachim than all of them without.

chunks.en: The bulls, the rams and the lambs
chunks.st: Failure to sacrifice one of the bulls, the rams, the sheep, or the goats of the additional offerings brought on Festivals

chunks.en: do not hold each other back.
chunks.st: does not prevent the sacrifice of the others.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: If they had many bulls
chunks.st: If the Temple treasurers had sufficient funds for the numerous bulls that are required to be sacrificed on that day

chunks.en: but did not have nesachim,
chunks.st: but they did not also have sufficient funds for the accompanying libations,

chunks.en: they should bring one bull and its nesachim,
chunks.st: they should rather bring one bull and its libations,

chunks.en: and not bring all of them without nesachim.
chunks.st: and they should not sacrifice all of them without libations.

summary: On Shavuos the two loaves come with two lambs. Rabbi Akiva says the loaves hold back the lambs, but Shimon ben Nanas says the lambs hold back the loaves, because in the midbar they brought lambs without loaves. Rabbi Shimon agrees with Ben Nanas, but for a different reason: lambs can be brought alone, but the loaves need the lambs to make them allowed.
stIntro: On Shavuot there is an obligation to sacrifice burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings together with the offering of the two loaves. The burnt offerings consists of a bull, two rams, and seven sheep. A goat is brought for the sin offering. Two sheep are brought as peace offerings and waved together with the two loaves.

chunks.en: The bull, the rams, the lambs and the goat
chunks.st: Failure to sacrifice the bull, the rams, and the sheep, which are all brought as burnt offerings, and the goat that is brought as a sin offering,

chunks.en: do not hold back the loaves,
chunks.st: does not prevent the bringing of the two loaves, and they are sacrificed nevertheless.

chunks.en: and the loaves do not hold them back.
chunks.st: Failure to bring the two loaves does not prevent sacrifice of the accompanying animal offerings.

chunks.en: The loaves hold back the lambs,
chunks.st: Failure to bring the two loaves prevents sacrifice of the accompanying peace offering of two sheep,

words.note: The two lambs brought with the loaves.

chunks.en: but the lambs do not hold back the loaves.
chunks.st: but failure to sacrifice the two sheep does not prevent the bringing of the two loaves;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

words.note: Rabbi Akiva ben Yosef, a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Shimon ben Nanas said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas says:

chunks.en: Not so!
chunks.st: No,

chunks.en: Rather, the lambs hold back the loaves,
chunks.st: rather the opposite is true. Failure to sacrifice the peace offering of two sheep prevents the bringing of the two loaves,

chunks.en: but the loaves do not hold back the lambs.
chunks.st: but failure to bring the two loaves does not prevent sacrifice of the accompanying peace offering of two sheep.

chunks.en: For this is what we find:
chunks.st: As we found

chunks.en: When the Jewish people were in the midbar for forty years,
chunks.st: that when the Jewish people were in the wilderness for forty years after the exodus from Egypt,

chunks.en: they brought lambs without loaves.
chunks.st: they sacrificed the two sheep as a peace offering on Shavuot without the two loaves,
chunks.stMore: as the two loaves may be brought only from wheat grown in Eretz Yisrael after the Jewish people entered the land.

chunks.he: אַף כָּאן יִקְרְבוּ כְבָשִׂים בְּלֹא לָחֶם.
chunks.en: So here too, they may bring lambs without loaves.
chunks.st: Here too, whenever wheat is unavailable, they should sacrifice the two sheep without the two loaves. However, the two loaves are not sacrificed without the peace offering of two sheep.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: The halachah is like Ben Nanas,
chunks.st: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas
chunks.stMore: that failure to sacrifice the two sheep prevents the bringing of the two loaves but failure to bring the two loaves does not prevent sacrifice of the accompanying peace offering of two sheep,

chunks.en: but the reason is not like he said.
chunks.st: but the reason for that ruling is not in accordance with his statement.

chunks.en: Because everything that is said in Sefer Bamidbar
chunks.st: As all the offerings that must be sacrificed on Shavuot that are stated in the book of Numbers
chunks.stMore: (see 28:27), i.e., two bulls, one ram, and seven sheep as additional offerings and a goat as a sin offering,

chunks.en: was brought in the midbar,
chunks.st: were sacrificed when the Jewish people were in the wilderness.

chunks.en: and everything that is said in Sefer Vayikra
chunks.st: But all the offerings stated in Leviticus (see 23:18–20), i.e., the offerings accompanying the two loaves,

chunks.en: was not brought in the midbar.
chunks.st: were not sacrificed when the Jewish people were in the wilderness.
chunks.stMore: Not only were the two loaves not sacrificed, but the accompanying offerings, including the peace offering of the two sheep, were also not sacrificed,

chunks.en: Once they came into Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: because it was only when they arrived in Eretz Yisrael that

chunks.en: they brought both these and those.
chunks.st: these additional offerings and those offerings accompanying the two loaves were sacrificed.
chunks.stMore: Neither the additional offerings of Shavuot nor the two loaves, and the offerings that accompany them, were sacrificed in the wilderness, contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas.

chunks.en: So why do I say
chunks.st: Rather, for what reason do I nevertheless

chunks.en: that they may bring lambs without loaves?
chunks.st: say that the sheep should be sacrificed without the loaves, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas?

chunks.he: שֶׁהַכְּבָשִׂים מַתִּירִין אֶת עַצְמָן בְּלֹא לֶחֶם.
chunks.en: Because the lambs make themselves allowed without the loaves.
chunks.st: It is due to the fact that the sheep permit themselves,
chunks.stMore: as the sprinkling of their blood and the burning of the portions consumed on the altar renders it permitted to partake of their meat.

chunks.en: But loaves without lambs,
chunks.st: And why are the loaves not sacrificed without the sheep?

chunks.en: I have nothing to make them allowed.
chunks.st: It is because there is no item to permit the loaves, as the loaves are permitted only after the sheep are sacrificed.

summary: The tamid and musaf offerings do not hold each other back. If the morning tamid or ketores was not brought, the afternoon one is still brought. Rabbi Shimon adds that a new mizbeach, Shulchan or Menorah is first used in a special way.

chunks.en: The tamid offerings do not hold back the musaf offerings,
chunks.st: Failure to sacrifice the daily offerings does not prevent sacrifice of the additional offerings,

words.note: The korban brought every morning and afternoon.
Extra korbanos on Shabbos, Rosh Chodesh and Yom Tov.

chunks.en: and the musaf offerings do not hold back the tamid offerings,
chunks.st: and likewise, failure to sacrifice the additional offerings does not prevent sacrifice of the daily offerings.

chunks.he: וְלֹא הַמּוּסָפִים מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
chunks.en: and the musaf offerings do not hold each other back.
chunks.st: And failure to sacrifice some of the additional offerings on a day when more than one is sacrificed, e.g., if it was both Shabbat and the New Moon, does not prevent sacrifice of the other additional offerings.

chunks.en: If they did not bring a lamb in the morning,
chunks.st: If the priests did not sacrifice a lamb in the morning as the daily offering, nevertheless,

chunks.en: they should bring one in the afternoon.
chunks.st: they should sacrifice a lamb in the afternoon
chunks.stMore: as the daily offering, as failure to sacrifice one daily offering does not prevent sacrifice of the other. In all of these cases, if they failed to sacrifice one offering, they should still sacrifice the other.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ אֲנוּסִין אוֹ שׁוֹגְגִין.
chunks.en: When is this? When they could not help it, or made a mistake.
chunks.st: When does this halakha apply? It applies at a time when the failure to sacrifice the daily morning offering was because they were prevented from sacrificing it due to circumstances beyond their control or they failed to sacrifice it unwittingly.

chunks.en: But if they did it on purpose
chunks.st: But if the priests acted intentionally

chunks.en: and did not bring a lamb in the morning,
chunks.st: and did not sacrifice a lamb in the morning as the daily offering,

chunks.en: they should not bring one in the afternoon.
chunks.st: they should not sacrifice a lamb in the afternoon as the daily offering.
chunks.stMore: Incense was burned twice a day, half a measure in the morning and half a measure in the afternoon.

chunks.en: If they did not burn ketores in the morning,
chunks.st: If they did not burn the half-measure of incense in the morning,

words.note: The special incense burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: they should burn it in the afternoon.
chunks.st: they should burn the half-measure in the afternoon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: And then all of it was brought in the afternoon,
chunks.st: And in such a case, the entire measure was sacrificed in the afternoon.

chunks.en: because they do not begin using
chunks.st: The reason for the difference between the daily offerings and the incense is that the daily service on a new

chunks.en: the golden mizbeach except with the ketores of spices,
chunks.st: golden altar is initiated only with the burning of the incense of the spices in the afternoon, at which time they would burn a full measure.

chunks.he: וְלֹא מִזְבַּח הָעוֹלָה אֶלָּא בְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר,
chunks.en: and not the mizbeach of the olah except with the morning tamid,
chunks.st: And the daily service on a new altar of the burnt offering, on which the daily offerings were sacrificed, is initiated only with the daily morning offering.

words.note: The outer mizbeach, where olah offerings are burned.

chunks.he: וְלֹא אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן אֶלָּא בְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: and not the Shulchan except with the lechem hapanim on Shabbos,
chunks.st: And use of a new Table was initiated only with the arrangement of the shewbread on Shabbat,

words.note: The golden table in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and not the Menorah except
chunks.st: and use of a new Candelabrum was initiated only with

chunks.en: with its seven lamps in the afternoon.
chunks.st: the kindling of its seven lamps in the afternoon.

summary: The Kohen Gadol brings a mincha every day, half in the morning and half in the afternoon. If he died after the morning half, the new Kohen Gadol brings a whole new issaron and burns half. If no new Kohen Gadol was chosen yet, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehuda argue who pays for it.

chunks.en: The griddle-cakes of the Kohen Gadol
chunks.st: The twelve loaves of matza prepared from a tenth of an ephah of flour of the griddle-cake offering of the High Priest

words.note: Flat cakes made in a pan.

chunks.en: were not brought in halves,
chunks.st: did not come from the house of the High Priest in halves.

chunks.en: but he brings a whole issaron,
chunks.st: Rather, the High Priest brings from his house a complete tenth of an ephah of flour (see Leviticus 6:13)

chunks.en: and splits it, and brings half in the morning
chunks.st: and divides it in half, and he sacrifices half in the morning

chunks.en: and half in the afternoon.
chunks.st: and half in the afternoon.

chunks.en: If a Kohen Gadol brought half in the morning and died,
chunks.st: In the case of a High Priest who brings and sacrifices half in the morning and dies,

chunks.en: and they appointed another Kohen in his place,
chunks.st: and they appointed another High Priest in his stead,

chunks.en: he should not bring half an issaron from his house,
chunks.st: the replacement High Priest should neither bring half of a tenth of an ephah of flour from his house

chunks.en: and not the half issaron of the first one,
chunks.st: nor sacrifice the remaining half of the tenth of an ephah of his predecessor.

chunks.en: but he brings a whole issaron,
chunks.st: Rather, he brings from his house an entire tenth of an ephah

chunks.en: and splits it, and brings half,
chunks.st: and divides it in half, sacrifices half,

chunks.en: and half is lost.
chunks.st: and the other half is not sacrificed and is lost.

chunks.en: So two halves are brought,
chunks.st: Consequently, two halves of a tenth of an ephah are sacrificed, one-half of what was brought by each priest,

chunks.en: and two halves are lost.
chunks.st: and the other two halves are lost.

chunks.en: If they did not appoint another Kohen,
chunks.st: If they did not appoint another High Priest in his stead,

chunks.en: whose money was it brought from?
chunks.st: from whose property was the griddle-cake offering brought and sacrificed?

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: From the money of the community.
chunks.st: It is brought and sacrificed from the property of the community.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: From the money of his heirs.
chunks.st: It is brought and sacrificed from the property of the heirs of the High Priest.

words.note: His children, who inherit his things.

chunks.en: And it was brought whole.
chunks.st: And for the duration of the period until a new High Priest was appointed, the griddle-cake offering was sacrificed as a complete tenth of an ephah of fine flour.
